profile_md:
## Carmeuse Americas (Carmeuse Group) — investor profile

**Overview.** Carmeuse Americas, headquartered in Pittsburgh, is the North and South American arm of Carmeuse Group, a privately held Belgian lime, limestone and (since 2025) cement group controlled by the Collinet family, with Cobepa holding a ~20% minority stake since 2005. In North America Carmeuse describes itself as the largest producer of lime and limestone products, running "28 manufacturing facilities in the USA and Canada" with "over 2,000 employees". Carmeuse Americas as a whole (including Brazil, Colombia and new Chilean/Argentine assets) cites "over 2,500 employees" and 30+ production facilities. **Plainly, this is a lime and minerals company, not a water treatment chemicals company.** Lime is a real municipal water/wastewater reagent (softening, pH adjustment, coagulation aid, biosolids stabilization, acid-mine and industrial wastewater neutralization), but for Carmeuse water is a small outlet. Steel fluxing, flue-gas desulfurization, chemicals and industrial uses, and construction are much larger.

**History and ownership.** Carmeuse was founded in Liège in 1860 and is headquartered in Louvain-la-Neuve. It entered North America in 1992 and bought six limestone/lime companies with 14 locations around the Great Lakes during the 1990s (Marblehead, Dravo-heritage plants and others). The defining US deal was the 2008 take-private of Oglebay Norton (O-N Minerals) for about $520m ($36/share), which added 13 eastern and Great Lakes locations, including the Rogers City (Calcite) quarry and the Strasburg VA plant. It lifted North American revenue to roughly $900m (Bus-Ex, 2008). Later North American add-ons were in services and equipment: STT Enviro Corp in 2017 (lime slaking and chemical make-up systems, rebranded Carmeuse Systems in 2024) and, through the soil-stabilization reagents subsidiary Mintek Resources, Omni Materials in December 2025 (13 LKD/quicklime/cement transload terminals). The group's recent large deals are in Latin America: 97.1% of Chile's Cementos Bío Bío (closed September 2025, ~$505m offer, ~$400m revenue, 960 staff) and a controlling stake in Argentina's Caleras San Juan (September 2026).

**Products and chemistries.** Everything is made in-house from owned quarries. The range covers high-calcium and dolomitic quicklime, hydrated lime, lime kiln dust, pulverized limestone for FGD, chemical-grade and aggregate limestone, and (via CBB) cement and ready-mix concrete. Water-relevant products are quicklime and hydrated lime for drinking-water softening and pH/alkalinity control, wastewater and biosolids treatment, and industrial and mining effluent neutralization. Carmeuse Systems (US: Storage & Transfer Technologies) sells lime slakers, silos and chemical feed systems to municipal and industrial water plants. That is an equipment business, excluded from chemical revenue.

**End markets.** The North American plants cluster around the Great Lakes and Ohio Valley steel belt, so steel is the largest customer sector and utility FGD is second (Bus-Ex). Other outlets are chemicals and industry (PCC, glass, pulp and paper, sugar), construction and soil stabilization (Mintek), mining, agriculture and water treatment. USGS consistently ranks water treatment as a minor outlet behind steel, chemical and industrial uses, FGD and construction.

**Footprint.** USGS's 2022 lime directory lists 16 Carmeuse US lime plants: Saginaw and Calera AL; Black River (Butler) and Maysville KY; Pelican (Baton Rouge) LA; River Rouge MI; Grand River, Huron, Maple Grove (Bettsville) and Millersville OH; Annville PA; Luttrell TN; Winchester (Clear Brook) and Strasburg VA; Manitowoc WI; and Buffington (Gary) IN. On top of these are limestone quarries such as Rogers City MI, the Canadian plants (Dundas, Beachville and Blind River ON) and the Omni and Mintek terminal network.

**Financials.** Group turnover is €2.5bn in the 2026 Sustainability Insights report (2025 basis), up from ~€2.0bn (2024 report and the CBB announcement) and €1.8bn in 2022. That is about $2.8bn at 1.13 USD/EUR, and it includes at least a partial year of CBB. No regional split is published. We estimate Carmeuse Americas' North American revenue at about $1.15bn: ~$900m in 2008, grown with pricing and roughly 40-45% of pre-CBB group sales. US revenue is about $1.0bn (Canada ~10-12% of plants). EBITDA is not disclosed. We estimate ~$620m at a 22% margin, since lime peers run 20-35% or more. That figure is a placeholder, not sourced. **US water treatment revenue is estimated at ~$65m**: ~$1.0bn US × ~80% lime (vs. stone, logistics and systems) × ~8% water share of lime demand. That is roughly 2% of the platform.

**M&A strategy.** Carmeuse runs a family-controlled buy-and-build in lime and adjacent calcium chemistry. In North America it bolts on downstream services (feed systems, soil-stabilization logistics). Growth capital has recently gone to Latin America (Brazil 2017-2020, Chile 2025, Argentina 2026), vertical integration into cement, and decarbonization (a net-zero lime plant design).

**Competitive position.** Carmeuse is one of the "big three" US lime producers alongside Lhoist North America and Graymont, followed by Mississippi Lime and US Lime & Minerals. Lime is regional (costly to haul), quarry-backed and permit-constrained, which gives incumbents durable pricing. In water specifically, Carmeuse competes as a commodity reagent supplier to municipal softening and wastewater plants, often through bids.

**Risks.** Steel exposure (blast furnace to EAF shift lowers flux lime per ton), coal-plant retirements shrinking FGD demand, CO2 intensity (lime calcination is process-emission heavy; 11.2 Mt CO2 group-wide in 2025), energy costs, and leverage after the CBB and CSJ deals.

**Uncertainties.** There is no public regional revenue, EBITDA or product mix. The water share is an estimate from USGS end-use patterns. The €2.5bn may be pro forma for CBB. The US plant list comes from USGS 2022 and may have changed (idlings and sales).
